title: Wardens of the White - Caer Dineval (DISMANTLED)
description: The cult's public face looked like Auril/Uthessil worship, but the true power structure was a bargain gone wrong: Kadroth struck a deal with the Hoarfrost hag coven to seize Caer-Dineval, with Hethyl (one of the coven) as the real contact to Uthessil, not Kadroth. RESOLVED: the party fought into the cistern, dispatched Hethyl (fate likely death, not fully confirmed - see her entry) along with reanimated zombies and dangerous brown mold, freed Nirenoore and Falk, and recovered loot including Hethyl's Flying Staff and the Slow Mercy. Kadroth was captured by Trovus while fleeing and is facing justice. Crannoc Siever was saved from poisoning-induced exhaustion (see his entry) and is currently recovering in Lonelywood rather than back at the Caer. The castle is now effectively without clear leadership - Avarice (still in residence, see her entry) is a live candidate to fill that vacuum. The Codicil of the White was never physically here - see Uthessil's entry for the real mechanism, now tied to the rewritten Ch.5 (Hoarfrost confrontation, see Adventure Roadmap).

title: Kadroth - Grifter, Not True Believer (CAPTURED)
description: Tiefling cult fanatic who ran Caer-Dineval's day-to-day operations. TRUE BACKSTORY: fled Baldur's Gate after grifting trouble with the thieves' guilds, wandered into Icewind Dale, ended up in Targos selling himself to Speaker Naerth Maxildanarr as 'a man of action.' Naerth, finalizing his own compromise with Auril's forces and unwilling to personally risk dealing with hags, let Kadroth take that risk instead - and continued directing Kadroth's operation from Targos on an ongoing basis, not as a one-time handoff (confirmed under pressure from Joosep). Kadroth's deal with the Hoarfrost hag coven got him control of Caer-Dineval and little else; not suited for leadership, aware of it, won't admit it. Genuinely, mistakenly believed the ice statue of Auril in the cistern shrine WAS Uthessil - sincere belief, not a lie. Wouldn't kill Crannoc directly, hence the slow poisoning instead. Wore an immaculate Auril-attuned chardalyn pendant. CAPTURED while attempting to flee - Trovus is bringing him to Caer-Konig to face justice; whether his confession about Naerth becomes public depends on how that plays out.

title: Hethyl Arkorran - Bheur Hag (LIKELY DEFEATED, UNCONFIRMED)
description: Bheur hag, daughter of Grandmother Cottongrass, true communication link to Uthessil, stationed in Caer-Dineval's cistern. Promised a coven seat if Auntie Sedge (weakest of the Hoarfrost) died - could be persuaded to free Crannoc in exchange for Sedge's death. Used Zirael's captivity as psychological leverage against Nirenoore. Let slip to Nirenoore (now party-known - see Hethyl's Intel entry) her contempt for Kadroth, doubts about the statue being Uthessil, frustration at being stuck at the Caer, irritation at the slow poisoning, and fragments about 'the vault' and 'the key.' FOUGHT: Bill's repeated Stunning Strikes kept her from acting at all before the fight turned into a battle against 8 reanimated cistern zombies and dangerous brown mold. Nirenoore and Falk were freed from her captivity in the process. LIKELY DEFEATED but NOT explicitly confirmed dead vs. fled/captured - still needs a decision. This matters significantly for Ch.5: if she's dead, the negotiated path (trading Sedge's death for cooperation) is closed, and the Hoarfrost confrontation becomes a straight assault with no inside informant.

title: The Hoarfrost - Hag Coven (Sea of Moving Ice)
description: A coven of three hags - Grandmother Cottongrass (powerful Bheur hag, coven leader, Hethyl's mother), Auntie Felsenmeer (large, imposing Annis hag), and Auntie Sedge (sea hag, weakest) - lairing on an iceberg in the Sea of Moving Ice, collectively known as the Hoarfrost. They hold leverage over Caer-Dineval through Kadroth's bargain, and physically hold/control the real Uthessil - the actual mechanism behind Hethyl's communication with it, not just a metaphorical link. Generally aware of events across the Dale but never bothered informing Kadroth, content to let him manage his small bubble of influence while they held the real power. CONFIRMED: this coven's confrontation is now the rewritten Ch.5 of the campaign, replacing the published adventure's Island of Solstice/Auril's Abode chapter entirely (see Adventure Roadmap entry). The party needs to defeat the Hoarfrost to retrieve Uthessil, bring it to Caer-Dineval, and unlock the vault holding the Codicil of the White. Naerth has prior history with this coven (he dealt with them before handing the risk to Kadroth) - expect his full involvement to surface around this confrontation.

title: Speaker Crannoc Siever (SAVED, RECOVERING)
description: Town speaker of Caer-Dineval. Was being deliberately, slowly poisoned over months by a chardalyn amulet (a Slow Mercy or a twin of it) to disguise the cult's takeover as natural decline - it was backfiring by looking increasingly suspicious rather than convincing. He knew about 'the hag' (Hethyl, whom he'd personally encountered and been frightened into submission by once) but not the specifics of Kadroth's wider coven deal; he'd hired Kadroth as head manservant months ago, told his old servants had left and needed replacing, when in fact most were imprisoned in the cistern. RESOLVED: in danger of dying from exhaustion, the party convinced him to ride along via dogsled across the wild country to reach Morskaya and the Drowned Priest, taking a 'shortcut' that didn't save time but let them track and kill an ice troll, using its heart to help him survive the journey (see Ice Troll Heart entry). Arriving near Maer Dualdon in brutal weather, Morskaya's awakened moose called her and the Drowned Priest, who used his one-time Greater Restoration to clear Crannoc's exhaustion entirely. Crannoc now owes the party a major debt. He is NOT returning to Caer-Dineval yet - staying with Nimsy in Lonelywood to recover, which leaves Caer-Dineval currently leaderless (see Wardens of the White entry) and will likely mean more people learn of Morskaya's existence over time.

title: Avarice - Arcane Brotherhood Wizard (Caer-Dineval)
description: Albino tiefling wizard of the Arcane Brotherhood, occupying the castle's second floor (former Hethyl location - see the location-swap). Desk, white leather spellbook, red rug, narrow bed, freestanding mirror, a staff of frost against the wall. Familiar: ink-black crow Skelm. Her two gargoyles, Gargle and Gurgle, are out in the field specifically looking for Dzaan - a concrete tie to the Dzaan/simulacrum thread, not generic rival-spying. She's here specifically to gain access to Uthessil by deposing the hag coven's control over it, believing the Wardens have access to the Codicil of the White, necessary to locate and enter Ythryn. She's seen the Auril statue herself and correctly senses it isn't powerful - if it's an Aurilith at all, an especially weak one - but doesn't know why (she doesn't realize it's a conduit, not Uthessil itself; see Uthessil's entry). Her scheme - tricking the party into misidentifying a decoy artifact as 'the Aurilith' to take a key for herself - is likely to fail regardless of success, since she doesn't understand the true retrieval requirement (the real Uthessil must come from the hag coven). She'll help depose the coven if pressed and promised help finding Ythryn in return; otherwise stays mostly uninvolved. Discoverable clue in her room: Perception 15 spots a symbol (a warship beneath a tree-like tower) among her research; Intelligence/Memory 15 recalls the same symbol among Dzaan's belongings. Bill will automatically notice she's researching Netherese/Ythryn material. With Kadroth captured and the castle leaderless, she's a live candidate to fill the power vacuum.

title: Uthessil - Location and True Nature (RESOLVED)
description: Uthessil is held by the Hoarfrost hag coven at their iceberg lair, not physically present at Caer-Dineval. What Kadroth and the cult believed was Uthessil - the ice statue of Auril in the cistern shrine - is not the Aurilith itself, but a conduit tied to a dimensionally-locked vault behind it (holding the Codicil of the White). The vault only opens when the real Uthessil is physically presented to it. Kadroth's belief that the statue WAS Uthessil was a sincere mistake, not a lie. RESOLVED INCIDENT: Glix attempted to destroy the statue after mostly clearing the brown mold that kept it frozen - the attempt got him stunned, and the statue/conduit remains intact and unharmed. No further consequence materialized from the attempt. CONFIRMED SEQUENCING: retrieving the real Uthessil from the Hoarfrost is now locked in as the rewritten Ch.5 of the campaign, replacing the published Island of Solstice/Auril's Abode chapter (see Adventure Roadmap entry).

title: Caer-Dineval Castle Layout & Current Assignments
description: First floor: Great Hall, Sitting Room (Throob), Office (Kadroth's former spot), Kitchen (Karou Salafan, non-cultist cook, two goats), Servants' Quarters (cultists Huarwar and Tam Sharf - mute housemaid, reassigned from captive to cultist in this version), Kennel (Alassar, 8yo human kennelboy - also where Zirael was held among the dogs, alongside the party's own sled dogs), Courtyard, Guard Towers (Mere, 14yo tiefling, Kadroth's kin). Second floor: Crannoc's former room (was guarded by Yajath), Avarice's Room (per the location swap). Cistern: C16-19 as published (entry ladder, cold storage with wrapped cultist bodies, flooded cistern with rowboat and submerged guard corpses, hidden marble slab gate). C20, Shrine to Auril - the statue/Uthessil conduit, kept frozen by brown mold, which was mostly but not entirely destroyed by Glix during the fight (see Uthessil's entry for the resolved outcome). C21, Hethyl's Abode - resolved, fight occurred here, Nirenoore and Falk freed. C22 (iron lever), C23/C24 (deeper cistern, Crannoc's remaining imprisoned servants - Lanthis Alderdusk, Elprekt Norbrav, Mylbara Norbrav, Dassir Ravenscar) have NOT yet been reached or retrieved - still an open loose end. Fel Suparra's status/placement remains undetermined, absent from recent material. Glix is no longer trapped behind the mold as of later sessions - he rejoined the others off-screen before the Trovus/Kadroth/Crannoc material played out.

title: Hethyl Fight - Cistern Zombie Contingency (TRIGGERED)
description: Design note for the fight against Hethyl - CONFIRMED TRIGGERED. The twelve submerged guard corpses in the flooded cistern reanimated as 8 ice zombies and joined the fight after Hethyl was quickly neutralized by repeated Stunning Strikes. The brown mold in the shrine room proved the most dangerous element of the encounter. Joosep went down to the zombies but survived.

title: Danae Xotal - Thayan Agent (Lonelywood)
description: Barkeep at The Lucky Liar, the only tavern in Lonelywood. Secretly a Thayan agent working for Szass Tam, the most powerful lich in Thay - planted in Icewind Dale years ago to watch for enemies of Szass Tam seeking refuge in Ten-Towns. No one else in Ten-Towns knows her secret; those she's marked as enemies in the past have quietly vanished. Doesn't currently bear on the plot but is worth keeping documented. The tavern cleared out when Glix bragged (nat 20 persuasion) about supplying rum to the Northlook Inn, but the party's actual heroics (destroying an Aurilith) won her over - she's friendly toward them now. Can see through Glix's disguise.

title: Iriskree Harrowhill - Scrimshaw Shop Owner (Lonelywood)
description: Owns a scrimshaw shop in the town of Lonelywood. Outwardly a 'doughy spinster'; secretly a retired assassin. Party passed by but hasn't interacted with her directly - open for future development.

title: The Lucky Liar - Tavern Regulars (Lonelywood)
description: Patrons at The Lucky Liar during the party's overnight stay in Lonelywood: Panic, an older red-skinned tiefling man with long white hair; Elgin, a half-elf who gave Bill a cot; and Lenore, an older dwarven woman unswayed by Glix's attempt to sell her rocks. Light flavor NPCs, open for reuse.

title: Nimsy
description: Accompanied Joosep toward Lonelywood earlier in the campaign. Found the party irate that they hadn't brought her the head of the white moose, then was won over once she learned Zethryn had been destroyed. Currently hosting Crannoc Siever in Lonelywood during his recovery (see his entry) - likely to result in more people eventually learning of Morskaya's existence.

title: Mere - Kadroth's Kin (Caer-Dineval Gatekeeper)
description: A teenage tiefling (14 years old), kin to Kadroth, the only guard on rotation in the Guard Towers at the time the party arrived. Tricked by Glix's psychic communication into letting the party inside. Withheld his name to avoid getting in trouble for letting them in - the party still doesn't know it.

title: Umberlee Shrine - Lonelywood Hidden Temple
description: Hidden shrine to Umberlee maintained by Morskaya, opposing Auril's frozen stasis. Contains the drowning pool (resolved via Angajuk) and the Marble Gazebo ritual basin. RESOLVED: Glix helped Morskaya free the Drowned Priest. Morskaya promised to aid Glix if needed, healed him, then whipped up a maelstrom on Maer Dualdon - ongoing for as long as she's in the area, demonstrated firsthand as freezing rain 'like spears' during later travel. The Drowned Priest's one-time Greater Restoration was later used to save Crannoc Siever. Possible open connection, unconfirmed: this may be the first stirring of Zethryn's 'great wave' vision to Joosep.

title: Mama Chrys's Augury - Weal for the Spire Plan (Flux'thuun-Tinted)
description: Before leaving Lonelywood, Mama Chrys cast Augury on heading to the Lost Spire toward the party's goal of defeating 'the Rime' (their shorthand for ending Auril's winter). Result: Weal, visibly influenced by Flux'thuun, which reframed the reading to emphasize ongoing movement/process over any fixed destination. NOTE: the Spire itself has since been deliberately deferred past Ch.2 (see Adventure Roadmap) - this augury's framing arguably predicted that outcome, since it never locked the party into that specific destination being the answer.

title: Nirenoore - Wild Elf Ranger/Rogue (PC)
description: Player character (Arianna), Ranger 4/Rogue 2 (Hunter). Tracked her wolf companion Zirael to Caer-Dineval, staked out the castle for days, was captured during a solo attempt to force her way in, and held as a 'pet' by Hethyl in a hidden cistern chamber - used as leverage and false hope of reunion. Freed by the party along with fellow captive Falk. Relayed everything Hethyl had let slip during captivity to the party (see Hethyl's Intel entry). Participated in the Elk Tribe cave raid alongside Mama Chrys, Joosep, and Falk. Open/undeveloped: Zirael's unusual age/intelligence has no locked explanation; a possible tie to Fenmarel Mestarine has been floated as flavor, not confirmed.

title: Zirael - Wolf Companion (Nirenoore)
description: Nirenoore's wolf companion. Retconned as one of the dogs in Caer-Dineval's courtyard kennel, tended by Alassar, alongside the party's own sled dogs. Captured with intent to be trained; unusually intelligent - firbolg animal-empathy (Mama Chrys, Joosep) picked up on this as the hook toward discovering Nirenoore's captivity. Used successfully during the Elk Tribe raid (alongside a second wolf/sled dog) to distract the white dragon wyrmlings Gelym and Tyzar, letting the raiding party sneak in undetected. Stat block: standard wolf (AC 13, HP 11, Speed 40 ft., STR 12/DEX 15/CON 12/WIS 12/CHA 6) with INT raised from 3 to 10 to reflect his unusual intelligence (understands Common and Elvish but can't speak); Bite attack's knockdown effect only applies against targets Large or smaller.

title: Falk - Elk Tribe Captive, Freed
description: Elk Tribe member held alongside Nirenoore in Hethyl's cistern lair - was to be sacrificed by Hethyl if a fight broke out. Freed by the party along with Nirenoore. Was originally sent by his tribe to Ten-Towns to beg for outside help against the chardalyn berserker corruption spreading through the Elk Tribe, but was waylaid and captured at Caer-Dineval before delivering his message. Finally completed that errand by leading Mama Chrys, Joosep, and Nirenoore to the Cave of the Berserkers, where the corruption source was dealt with (see Chardalyn Berserkers entry). Absent from the subsequent Cackling Chasm session.

title: Hethyl's Flying Staff (Loot)
description: Wondrous item, uncommon, no attunement required. A slender white staff, cold to the touch and faintly rimed with frost, looted from Hethyl. Command word (action) makes it hover beside the holder or stop hovering/fall; bonus action to mount it (one additional Medium or smaller creature can ride behind); once mounted, an action commands it to fly up to 50 feet in any direction. Drops if not held or mounted. Given to Mama Chrys.

title: Joosep - Circle Shiverveil Ranger
description: Firbolg Ranger (Marvin). Broke his connection to Zethryn for a +1/+1 bonus against intelligent Auril-servants. Privately suspects Wynnette's true nature but hasn't told the party. Lost Vega Shiverveil to Auril's retaliation after Zethryn's destruction. Went down to zombies at Caer-Dineval, survived; went down twice during the Elk Tribe cave raid, revived both times by Mama Chrys - a repeating near-death pattern worth watching, especially relevant to the still-undeveloped unconsciousness/stakes homebrew mechanic. See Joosep's Secret entry (DM-facing only, not party knowledge) regarding the Elk Tribe raid. Absent from the Caer-Dineval resolution session and the Cackling Chasm session.

title: Speaker Naerth Maxildanarr - Zhentarim Leader
description: Former Luskan rogue, secretly head of Zhentarim in Ten-Towns, wants to make Targos a trade hub for the Black Network. Commands 12+ spies throughout Ten-Towns, uses three flying snakes to relay messages. Accepts bribes to exempt specific citizens from Targos's sacrifice rotation. Glix has openly wanted him dead; the party deprioritized this - still a live, unresolved tension. CONFIRMED: has a deal with the Hoarfrost hag coven, and used Kadroth as a disposable proxy to avoid personal risk, continuing to direct Kadroth's operation at Caer-Dineval on an ongoing basis from Targos rather than a one-time handoff - making his Zhentarim network directly complicit in the Caer-Dineval situation. With Kadroth captured by Trovus, Naerth will almost certainly learn his operation has been exposed very quickly. Given the party's trajectory into Ch.3 soon, the practical result is that he won't bother maintaining secrecy by the time the party reaches Ch.5 (the Hoarfrost confrontation, replacing the published Island of Solstice chapter) - expect him to be upfront about his goals and affiliations once that point is reached, rather than continuing to hide. This sets up a likely major Naerth confrontation or reveal scene around Ch.5, tied directly to his own prior history with the coven.

title: Hethyl's Intel - Party-Known
description: Nirenoore relayed to the whole party what Hethyl let slip during her captivity: contempt for Kadroth as an undeserving con man; that the ice statue in the Caer-Dineval shrine isn't really Uthessil; resentment at being stuck at the Caer instead of properly seated with her mother's coven; repeated wishes for Auntie Sedge's death to open a coven seat; contempt for Uthessil treating her as disposable; irritation that Crannoc's poisoning was taking too long; a sneering aside that the real power was never at the castle, but out on the ice; bitter, unexplained mutters about 'the vault' and 'the key'; and real fear, unlike her usual contempt, when the wider coven itself came up by name. All of this is now shared party knowledge.

title: Trovus - Caer-Konig Militia Leader
description: Caer-Konig militia figure, also associated with a gnoll bounty at Cackling Chasm (now fulfilled - see that entry). Confronted the Wardens of the White situation at Caer-Dineval, catching Kadroth attempting to flee and taking him into custody to face justice at Caer-Konig - not simply to rest, as first assumed. Whether Kadroth's confession about Naerth's involvement becomes public depends on how that plays out. Afterward, caught Glix, Keogr, and Bill up on everything learned since Hethyl's death, and pushed the party toward prioritizing the duergar/Sunblight threat next, offering the Cackling Chasm bounty as an interim, trust-building task - which the party completed. His handling of Kadroth's actual fate/justice is presumed to have proceeded off-screen; confirm outcome if it matters later, especially regarding Naerth's exposure.

title: The Slow Mercy (Item)
description: Wondrous item (chardalyn pendant), rare, requires attunement. A blade-shaped pendant of corrupted chardalyn, colder than the air around it - a crueler cousin of the Wardens' standard amulets, and very likely the actual method used to poison Crannoc Siever. As an action, the wearer can touch a creature and force a DC 13 Constitution saving throw; on a failure, the target gains one level of exhaustion at each subsequent dawn until cured by remove curse, greater restoration, or similar. Curse of Corruption: while attuned, roll a d6 at each dawn - on a 1, DC 12 Charisma save or move one step closer to Lawful Evil (deliberately left mysterious beyond that - track fails, don't reveal an endpoint). Iceheart Adhesion: the wearer may attune to it as an action, but unattuning requires a long rest spent by a warm fire. Currently held by Mama Chrys, deliberately kept unattuned.

title: Joosep's Secret - Falk's Kill (DM-FACING, PARTY DOES NOT KNOW)
description: SENSITIVE - handle carefully. During the Elk Tribe cave raid, Joosep secretly turned Falk's final blow against a subdued tribesman from nonlethal to lethal, without Falk's knowledge or consent. Only Mama Chrys witnessed this and knows the truth - the party believes both deaths were unavoidable casualties, not a deliberate, hidden escalation by one of their own. Sits on top of Joosep's ongoing grief (Vega's death, his severed Zethryn bond, repeatedly going down in recent fights) - whether this reads as cracking under strain, misplaced anger at the corrupted tribesmen, or something colder is intentionally undefined. Live risks: Mama Chrys sitting on this indefinitely, confronting Joosep privately, or it surfacing to the wider party - any could significantly affect party trust and Joosep's arc. Not to be revealed or hinted at outside DM planning.

title: DM Prep Checklist - Post-Session Tasks
description: COMPLETED: printable item sheets for the flying staff and Slow Mercy; Zirael's character sheet (standard wolf, INT raised to 10, knockdown restricted to Large or smaller); a narrated description for what the two wolves did to distract the wyrmlings during the Elk Tribe raid. STILL OPEN: a homebrew mechanic to make falling unconscious feel higher-stakes, requested by the players - increasingly relevant given Joosep's and now Bill's repeated close calls.

title: Chardalyn Berserkers - Elk Tribe (RESOLVED)
description: Deep Duerra psionic corruption - not demonic influence, not Auril's favor - affecting a splinter of the Elk Tribe (see that entry), likely from duergar chardalyn mining/theft bleeding into their territory, the same mechanism affecting Circle Blackgleam's crystal gardens elsewhere. The cave (former dwarf mining tunnels) housed a Deep Duerra psi-crystal shrine (see that entry) in place of the published module's divine brazier. RESOLVED: Falk led Mama Chrys, Joosep, and Nirenoore to the cave. They used two wolves (Zirael plus a second wolf/sled dog) to distract the white dragon wyrmlings Gelym and Tyzar, sneaking in undetected; knocked out the butcher and carefully extracted the psi-crystal from its altar before real fighting began, then subsequently destroyed it. Two tribesmen were subdued nonlethally and tied up; two died - one an unavoidable casualty, the other due to Joosep secretly turning a nonlethal blow lethal (see Joosep's Secret entry - not party knowledge). Duerra-attuned chardalyn was confiscated from survivors. DM note: berserker HP was scaled down for the reduced 4-person raiding party.

title: Deep Duerra Psi-Crystal (Cave of the Berserkers) - DESTROYED
description: Replaced the published module's Frostmaiden's Fire brazier - a fist-sized corrupted chardalyn crystal set into a small altar bearing Deep Duerra's symbol (a mind flayer skull), kept berserkers in the cave from dropping below 1 HP while active. RESOLVED: carefully extracted intact (DC 15 Arcana/Religion to spot it was socketed rather than fused, DC 13 Strength/thieves' tools to remove it safely) rather than destroyed on the spot - but the party subsequently destroyed it afterward anyway, permanently ending its effect.

title: Tribe of the Elk - Reghed Nomads
description: Largest and most outsider-tolerant of the four remaining Reghed tribes; tribe of the hero Wulfgar, son of Beornegar. Views Ten-Towners as 'tame folk.' King Jarund Elkhardt: nearly 50, terse, cautious after decades of rule; lost his only heir, Jarund Twice-Born, to a cave bear roughly a decade ago, succession uncertain. Deeply concerned about Auril's winter; his shaman Mjenir believes the only way to break the curse is to kill the goddess in her own home - a striking, unprompted echo of the campaign's own endgame roadmap. The tribe's fracturing under Deep Duerra chardalyn corruption has been resolved (see Chardalyn Berserkers entry) via Falk's intervention.

title: Oyaminartok - The Polar Werebear (MET)
description: CR 8 werebear, title/role handed down over generations, near-mythic progenitor of goliath werebears, predating both goliath settlements' claims on her. Eyepatch hides a cursed paralysis-gaze eye (not a missing eye); grants +3 Perception and shapechanger detection. During the winter, the burden of choosing new werebears has lapsed amid the settlements' squabbling - why Keogr was mauled by a rogue lycanthrope rather than ritually chosen. RESOLVED: finally met via a random encounter en route to Cackling Chasm. Her poor social skills made her a genuinely off-putting figure on first impression. Told Keogr his curse might be a gift, and implied that if he proves he's earned it, she can help him find/unlock it. Followed the party into the gnoll hideout afterward purely as an observer, apparently watching Keogr specifically. OPEN QUESTION: Keogr went on to personally kill the Gnoll Fang (Chyzka) during that fight - does this satisfy her 'prove yourself' condition, or does she want something more deliberate? Needs a decision before she comes up again. Other intel (Coldlight Walkers/Frostling connection, external Sunblight knowledge) hasn't come up yet but remains available.

title: Cackling Chasm - Underground Passage (RESOLVED)
description: Underground route with unstable ice and strange acoustics, tied to Trovus's gnoll bounty. RESOLVED: taken on as a reward-motivated side quest from Trovus. No party member shared a language with the gnolls inside. Glix scouted invisibly, found the Gnoll Fang (Chyzka), spored him, and attempted communication; Bill recognized Yeenoghu's symbol but didn't communicate this clearly, and a fight broke out despite the gnolls being individually weak (CR 1/2, buffed with two longbow attacks each). The chasm's terrain made positioning difficult, and roughly 5 critical hits turned the fight dangerous - two shove attacks knocked Bill 200 feet down into the chasm, where he failed two death saves before Mama Chrys revived him, only after falling 50 feet herself attempting the rescue. Keogr personally killed the Gnoll Fang. The party collected gnoll ears, fulfilling Trovus's bounty. Both Keogr and Bill came away with lingering injuries - see that entry.

title: Ice Troll Heart - Travel Resource
description: An ice troll was tracked and killed during the dogsled journey to save Crannoc Siever; its heart was used to help him survive the trip's exhaustion risk. Light worldbuilding note - may be a reusable survival resource for future desperate travel situations.

title: Chyzka - Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu (DECEASED)
description: Gnoll fang of Yeenoghu, leader of the gnoll band at Cackling Chasm. Glix found and spored him during invisible scouting and attempted peaceful contact, but a language barrier and Bill's unclear handling of recognizing Yeenoghu's symbol led to a fight instead of a parley. Killed by Keogr during the resulting battle - possibly satisfying Oyaminartok's 'prove yourself' test (see her entry, still an open question).

title: Lingering Injuries (Homebrew System)
description: Homebrew mechanic for serious injuries beyond normal HP loss. Confirmed results so far: 'Bruised' (Keogr - minor, flavor-level). 'Festering Wound' (Bill - ACTIVE AND ONGOING: max HP reduced by 1d3 per day until either 40+ HP of total healing is received, or a DC 15 Medicine check successfully performs surgery). Bill's wound needs active tracking at the table - it's a worsening condition, not a one-time penalty.

title: Bill - Human Monk (Hermit) - Festering Wound
description: Reads Netherese, learned Ythryn/Netheril lore from Polybeus's writings in his own hermitage (a Ythryn splinter). Carries an Oghma boon (auto-success on Netherese checks, escalation trigger still undefined) and the unresolved 'Auril-connection gap' - doesn't yet know Ythryn holds an Aurilith-killer. Became active after Waylen's death. SESSION UPDATE: fell 200 feet into Cackling Chasm after being shoved by gnoll crits, failed two death saves before Mama Chrys revived him. Came away with a Festering Wound (see Lingering Injuries entry) - max HP currently eroding by 1d3/day until treated. This is an active, urgent status effect, not resolved flavor text.

title: Campaign Status Snapshot (as of latest session)
description: Party is level 6+, Ch. 2, closing out the chapter. STRUCTURAL: the Lost Spire of Netheril will NOT happen this chapter - deliberately deferred. Cackling Chasm (now resolved) was the final Ch.2 side quest, taken specifically to delay the Ch.3 dragon-vs-dungeon decision point until Joosep returns. Ch.5 is confirmed rewritten to center on the Hoarfrost hag coven confrontation, replacing the published Island of Solstice/Auril's Abode chapter (see Adventure Roadmap entry) - this is also expected to be when Naerth Maxildanarr stops hiding his Zhentarim affiliations. Current active roster has fluctuated: Joosep absent for several recent sessions; Nirenoore and Falk absent from the most recent (Cackling Chasm). RESOLVED since the last major snapshot: the Caer-Dineval cult dismantled (Kadroth captured, Hethyl likely dead - unconfirmed, Crannoc saved via the Drowned Priest's Greater Restoration and currently recovering in Lonelywood); the Elk Tribe's chardalyn berserker corruption cleared; the party's first meeting with Oyaminartok; the Cackling Chasm gnoll bounty, including Bill's near-fatal 200-foot fall and new Festering Wound (active, urgent - see that entry). Major still-open threads: Hethyl's exact fate, the Hoarfrost/Uthessil retrieval (now Ch.5), Joosep's secret (Falk's death - DM-facing only), Avarice's scheme and Dzaan connection, Glix wanting Naerth dead, Glix's interrupted Zethryn vessel attunement, Crannoc's recovery creating a Caer-Dineval power vacuum, whether Oyaminartok's 'prove yourself' condition for Keogr has been satisfied, and the still-undeveloped unconsciousness/stakes homebrew mechanic. title: Codicil of the White
description: The true key to entering and navigating Ythryn's magic. Held in a dimensionally-locked vault at Caer-Dineval, behind the ice statue of Auril (a conduit, not Uthessil itself - see Uthessil's entry). The vault only opens when the real Uthessil, held by the Hoarfrost hag coven, is presented to it. CONFIRMED: retrieving it is the central goal of the rewritten Ch.5 (replacing Island of Solstice/Auril's Abode) - see Adventure Roadmap entry.

title: Adventure Roadmap - Chapter Structure
description: Consolidated campaign structure. Ch.1 Ten-Towns - complete. Ch.2 Icewind Dale - closing out (Lost Spire deliberately deferred past this chapter; Cackling Chasm was the final Ch.2 side quest). Ch.3/4 Sunblight Fortress / chardalyn dragon rampage - upcoming, pending Joosep's return for the dragon-vs-dungeon decision point. Ch.5 - CONFIRMED REWRITE: the published adventure's Island of Solstice/Auril's Abode chapter is replaced entirely with a confrontation against the Hoarfrost hag coven (see that entry) - retrieving the real Uthessil to unlock the vault at Caer-Dineval and obtain the Codicil of the White. Also the expected point where Naerth Maxildanarr stops hiding and becomes forthright about his goals and affiliations. Ch.6 Ythryn - retrieve what's needed to end Auril's winter, using the Codicil to navigate. Endgame: Auril Confrontation - destroying enough Auriliths draws her out directly. OPEN: whether any of the published Island of Solstice content (trials, relics) should be ported into the Hoarfrost rewrite is undecided - not urgent until Ch.5 prep begins.
